text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Crowds of consumers were seen swarming flour mills in different parts of the city and bread disappeared from bakeries as the wheat shortage in Karachi touched new heights.
- Two million pilgrims gathered to perform Haj as the death toll from a huge blaze that swept through tents soared to 343 people, mostly Asians.

- The Federal Investigation Agency has registered cases against 12 senior officials and businessmen who allegedly caused a colossal loss by exporting 100,000 tonnes of rice at a rate lower than the prevalent international market prices.

- The intelligence authorities arrested another Air Force officer believed to be an accomplice of Squadron Leader Mohammad Farooq who was arrested in the U.S. for smuggling heroin, a spokesman for the Pakistan Air Force said.
- A notorious smuggler was arrested in Rawalpindi with two kg of fine quality heroin, a pistol and a few samples of uranium used to make atomic bombs.
- A German tourist was arrested by the Anti Narcotics Force in the town of Taftan, a Pakistan-Iran border town, for smuggling 128 kg of hashish.
- Pakistan and the European Union will start talks on a new trade agreement in Brussels on April 24.

- Pakistan's major international donors have assured the government of their maximum support during fiscal 1997/98 (July-June) including a $1.5 billion extended structural adjustment facility, Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz said.

- Pakistan's fiscal deficit remained high which partly explains the double digit rate of inflation despite the fact that it had the best record of growth in Asia with an average of 6.1 percent in 1981-1990, the Economic and Social Survey of Asia and Pacific said.
- A ship carrying 12,163 tonnes of sugar is expected to arrive at the Karachi Port on Thursday.
BUSINESS RECORDER

- A Pakistani communication satellite system, to be called PAKSAT, will be launched at an estimated cost of $220 million.. Alcatel Espace will launch the satellite on behalf of Pakistan under a 15-year licence.

- In line with government policy to downsize state-owned organisations, the Karachi Electric Supply Corporation has decided to lay off another 2,000 workers and 110 officers, sources said. KESC has already sacked 203 workers and 40 officers.
- Credit Lyonnais Securities Asia has advised its clients to sell PTCL shares.
THE NEWS

- Pakistan International Airline Investment Ltd (PAIL) suffered a major setback when its equity partner in leasehold interests of the airline-managed company, Prince Faisal, purchased the freehold interests of the PAIL-owned Scribe hotel in Paris without consulting PAIL's other 50 percent stakeholder.
- The first summit of the D-8 group, comprising eight developing Moslem countries, including Pakistan, may take place on June 14-15.
- Pakistani test opener Aamir Sohail was banned for two years by the Pakistan Cricket Board for defaming certain officials and team-mates in a March 23 interview with The News.
